name: Jinx
notes: The fight opens with Jinx already toggled to Fishbones, since a real player switches before engaging.

Super Mega Death Rocket has a 0.6s cast time (Jinx is busy, no other cast or attack starts) and is fired at t=0 assumed from beyond its ~1500-unit maximum-damage travel distance, so after that cast time it lands doing its full, maximally-travelled damage; this resolves the dossier's highest-impact open question toward best-case play.

Zap! and Super Mega Death Rocket! both have a 0.6s cast time that keeps Jinx busy (no other cast, no attack) until it ends; their damage lands only after a further delay (Zap!'s cast-time-scaled cast, and the rocket's travel time) modeled as their own events, and Flame Chompers! has no cast time so it costs nothing but still waits for a cast in progress.

Flame Chompers are thrown directly under the stationary dummy; since the dummy never walks onto them, they are assumed to still detonate as soon as they arm (0.4s to land + 0.5s to arm = 0.9s after cast) rather than waiting out their 5s self-destruct timer.

Fishbones' 110% AD hit is modeled as the engine's normal 100% AD basic attack plus a 10% AD on-hit rider, both crit-affected, costing 20 mana per attack from the build's total mana pool (no regeneration is modeled); once that pool runs dry Jinx toggles back to the free Pow-Pow stance and keeps attacking for the rest of the fight.
Because the rotation never switches back to Fishbones after that one mana-driven swap to Pow-Pow, the dossier's open question of whether Rev'd up stacks survive a stance switch never arises here.

Rev'd up is modeled as a single duration shared by all current stacks (each Pow-Pow attack refreshes it and adds a stack up to 3) rather than each stack expiring independently, since continuous attacking in this fight never lets a partial stack lapse.

Fishbones' attack-speed penalty is applied as -10% of the build's own bonus attack speed stat, since the engine only exposes the kit's own additive attack-speed contribution rather than a multiplier on the whole bonus AS pool.

Zap! and Flame Chompers! are cast on cooldown throughout the fight; Super Mega Death Rocket's 45-85s cooldown is far longer than the fight and is not expected to come off cooldown again, though the driver supports a recast if a build's ability haste ever allows it.
Get Excited! is not modeled: its movement/attack speed burst only triggers on a champion takedown, which a stationary dummy with a fixed health pool is not expected to provide within the fight.

Zap!, Flame Chompers!, and Super Mega Death Rocket! draw from the same tracked mana pool as Fishbones attacks; if the pool runs out before one of them is ready, that ability simply stops being cast for the rest of the fight.
